<!-- pr-reviewer: 109043405eb3c48f617862676c3d9543eb5ace53 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge**

**What looks good**
- The collision envelope is never smaller than the modelled body. `HolderProfile::envelope` (`crates/tools/src/holder_profile.rs`) clips every facet exactly to each axial band and takes the farthest clipped vertex. The max of the convex radius over a convex polygon sits at a vertex, so a facet that crosses a band with no vertex inside it still counts. Band edges are inclusive on both sides, merging only takes the larger radius, and there is a 1e-6 pad. The unit tests pin this: a sliver facet, and a randomized "no point of any facet outside its band".
- The one-cylinder laws use `enclose()`. It widens the shank to the widest reach beside it, and the holder is as wide as the widest band above the shank and runs to the body's top. A body reaching into the flutes is refused by name rather than approximated.
- Every consumer of the holder dimensions goes through `tool_body::judged`: `collect_job` (generation, dodge, drill reach), `posting::fixture_problems` and `machine::check_document`. The other `tool_of` callers only read diameter or kind, so I found no path that judges the smaller cylinder. The fixture laws take the exact band stack (`bands_vs_fixtures_held`, `rapids_vs_fixtures_held`, `posed_steel::sweep`), including the shank carried up to a body's foot, and the spindle housing rides on the body's top.
- With no body the stack equals the old `holder_len`/`holder_radius` sums, and the stamp adds bytes only when a body exists. The existing goldens did not move.
- Degenerate input refuses by name at the command (`SetToolBody::new`), again at use (`judged`) and again on project load (`validate.rs`). The new files have no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic`. Casts are bounded by the 500 mm and 2000 mm caps and the 2048-band clamp.
- `SetToolBody` is undoable, with a snapshot prev/next. `DeleteTool` and `EditTool` carry the body, and an edit that would put the body over the flutes is refused. The component is in `schema.rs`.
- Project v58 is optional and additive: absent means none, there is no rewrite, and the envelope is re-derived on load so file and judgement cannot disagree.
- Process is clean: provenance lines, `docs/decisions/368-tool-body-step.md`, a `Changelog:` line, `Fixes #368`, no `CHANGELOG.md` edit, no build.rs, workflow, script or dependency changes.

**Local results (PR trial-merged with current main, clean merge, own target dir)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --no-run` | builds |
| tools lib | 15 passed |
| app `tool_body` | 8 passed |
| app `setup_relative`, `setup_stock_source` | 8, 6 passed |
| app `project_roundtrip`, `posting`, `commands_undo` | 69, 17, 32 passed |
| app `fixtures`, `machine`, `drill_reach`, `rotary_fixtures`, `posed_contact`, `carried_fixtures_cache` | 14, 32, 6, 4, 5, 6 passed |
| sim `posed_fixture`, `posed_fixture_midpose`, `posed_rapids`, `vertical_rapids`, `sideways_rapids` | 7, 3, 5, 16, 3 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

I did not run the UI suites. The PR leaves `crates/ui` untouched, and the body is reachable only through the command and the project file.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
1. The one-cylinder laws (rest reach, solid law, dodge, drill reach, max tool length) use the enclosing cylinder, so a stepped holder can over-report there. That is the safe direction, and the maintainer's decision list already records it.
2. `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` was already over the 400-line target (3173 lines) and grows by a few lines. This is not blocking.
3. A v58 file is refused by an older reader. That is deliberate and documented in `file.rs`, and it is not marked breaking. The maintainer may want to confirm that reading.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
